findings: Design review added a separate two-integer advisory-lock namespace for receipt IDs after the common owner lock. It serializes v2 creators sharing a global receipt ID before duplicate detection, preserving unique insert and negative-write ordering. Legacy writers do not take this lock; no native or full cutover guarantee is claimed.

The first actual SQL run passed 74 of 76 cases. Two fixture setups violated existing parent/issuance foreign keys before reaching the intended denial: deleting a referenced parent, and assigning a binding to an absent alternate parent. The corrected fixtures use an absent requested parent identity and an actually observed alternate parent. No SQL constraint or implementation behavior was weakened. The expanded suite adds both cross-owner collision orderings and an old proof writer before and after the additive column to check cached rowtype compatibility.

The primary transport suite passed 75/75 on its first run. Initial TypeScript diagnostics exposed one Object.fromEntries fixture annotation and readonly mutations in the new SQL fixture; only test types were corrected. Initial independent composition passed one of two cases because its fixture overlooked the unchanged admission bridge's immediate inspect after claim. The corrected case verifies denial during that automatic post-claim check. Initial logs are preserved; no existing source or tests changed.

Root and independent review found no remaining source blocker. The new full protocol-2 proof cannot complete the unchanged v1 admission flow; deliberate exact cleanup remains available. Final focused/full tests, strict types/scoped lint and production build pass on frozen source. Proof storage is distinct from versioned consumption and atomic capacity admission, which remain unfinished. Real Auth, native concurrency and provider/device evidence remain separate.
